structural.name: Notice · not in version history
structural.text: Not covered by version history. Custom domains are stored on the server, not in the project file, so restoring an earlier version of the site leaves domains exactly as they are now — History's “nothing is lost” applies to General, SEO, Analytics and Custom code only.
structural.why: UX-I-40 — half of Settings is inside version history and half is outside it, and nothing says which

structural.name: Notice · saves immediately
structural.text: Saved as you go. Every action on this screen writes to the server the moment you press it — there is nothing buffered, so this screen shows no savebar and never reports unsaved changes.
structural.why: UX-I-36 — one savebar over three different commit models; a section that writes immediately must say so and not render the bar

structural.name: Open decision · nav grouping
structural.text: OPEN DECISION — group names and membership. UX-I-37 asks for the groups to be renamed into the user's vocabulary and for two rows to move: “PLUMBING” is an implementer's word, Analytics is not distribution and Forms is not plumbing. Proposed: SITE (General, Branding, SEO, Canvas) · PUBLISHING (Export, Domains, Redirects, Localization) · VISITORS (Analytics, Forms) · ADVANCED (Custom code, Headers, Integrations, Webhooks) · WORKSPACE ↗ (Members, Billing). Drawn, not applied — renaming a group also rewrites the breadcrumb on 30 section boards, so it lands as one decision or none.
structural.why: UX-I-37 — group rename is a founder-level naming call and it invalidates 30 breadcrumbs; drawn as an open decision rather than half-applied
